summary: An 1853 circular tower on Pond Island at the mouth of Narraguagus Bay, Maine; a rescue in 1929, sold in 1934, and still private.

lens.note: Fifth-order Fresnel lens fitted in 1856 (Lighthouse Friends); NRHP says the lens has been removed; Archive lists the optic as removed.

structures.note: Circular tower, nearly 31 ft (9.5 m) to the lantern centre; reinforced in brick in 1894; ten-sided lantern dating to 1876 (NRHP). The Archive gives granite blocks as the tower material; Lighthouse Friends calls it cylindrical.
One-and-a-half-storey keeper's house, clapboarded, joined to the tower by an L-shaped workroom (NRHP).

staffing.note: Discontinued 21 June 1933 per Lighthouse Friends, replaced by a lighted bell buoy 575 yards away; NRHP and Archive give 1934.

access.note: Privately owned since the 1934 sale; the Archive lists it as not open to the public; Lighthouse Friends says grounds, dwelling and tower are closed.

visit.note: Best seen from the water; tour boats pass the island.

events.note: Congress appropriated $4,000 on 3 March 1851 for a lighthouse on the east side of Pond Island (Lighthouse Friends)
Tower and first dwelling built 1853 (NRHP); the Archive dates the station's establishment to 1853
Fifth-order Fresnel lens replaced seven lamps and 21-inch reflectors; the light stayed fixed white
New one-and-a-half-storey frame keeper's house built; Lighthouse Friends gives the Board's 1875 description of the old dwelling as uninhabitable
Tower deck replaced and ten-sided lantern dates to 1876 (NRHP); Lighthouse Friends dates the new deck and lantern to 1875
North wing of the old brick dwelling converted to a workroom; cellar and cistern built; brick covered way to the new house
Tower walls reinforced with brick and a new iron lantern deck provided (Board annual report); the tower's diameter increased to its present size (NRHP)
Act approved 6 June 1900 appropriated $150 to buy land for a new boat landing
Old boathouse and boat slip moved to the new landing (Lighthouse Friends)
Crew of the Canadian schooner Valdare sheltered at the station; keeper Charles E. Tracy cared for them until 16 August and was commended
Discontinued 21 June 1933; lighted bell buoy established 575 yards away (Lighthouse Friends)
Sold at auction to Wilbur Dameron (Lighthouse Friends); NRHP says sold to a private citizen
Nomination received by the National Register in October 1987; reference 87002022; listed under the Light Stations of Maine multiple-property submission

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends gives 21 June 1933 as the date the light was discontinued (bell buoy 575 yards away); the NRHP nomination and the Archive both give 1934 for deactivation. The sale at auction in 1934 is agreed. The record's 1934 follows the two sources, so no correction is proposed; the story gives both.
Lighthouse Friends (put into service April 1853), the NRHP nomination (erected 1853) and the Archive (established 1853) agree on 1853.

The story states both: the nomination describes a circular brick tower reinforced in brick in 1894, and the Archive gives granite blocks. Lighthouse Friends says cylindrical. No source read settles the material.
Lighthouse Friends dates the new deck and lantern to 1875; the NRHP gives 1876 for the deck and the lantern. The story gives both.

Lighthouse Friends says the Maine superintendent of lights supervised construction; the NRHP form names the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers as designer. The story reports both as stated; no source read settles it.

notes_for_editor: Rich station. Cross-checked: the 1894 Board repair entry (n4) is in the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1894, printed p. 41 (checked on the page image; scan 346). The boat-slip item (n5) is in the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1897, printed p. 40, and the Jerry Ledge bell buoy is in the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1896, printed p. 18; the earlier draft wrongly put both in one report, and the story now separates them. The 1896-1897 and 1900 volumes have no page index, so the cites give printed pages from the OCR text and no scan page. Deactivation conflict: Lighthouse Friends says discontinued 21 June 1933 with a bell buoy 575 yards away; the NRHP nomination and the Archive both give 1934 for deactivation. The sale to Dameron is 1934 in both. The record's deactivated 1934 is a choice between sources, shown as a correction for a human to decide. Lantern: NRHP 1876 vs Lighthouse Friends 1875 (deck and lantern). Keeper's house demolition: NRHP says part of the house was removed nine years after 1875; Lighthouse Friends and the Board corpus give 1887 for the conversion; the story uses 1887 from Lighthouse Friends. Tower material: NRHP brick; Archive granite blocks; Lighthouse Friends cylindrical; the story states the NRHP and Archive versions. Designer: NRHP names the Army Corps of Engineers as designer; Lighthouse Friends says the Maine superintendent of lights supervised construction; the story reports both as stated. The NRHP copy read has the Keeper's decision block blank, so the listing is described as a nomination under the Light Stations of Maine multiple-property listing, not as a confirmed listing; the record's nrhp_listed event rests on the nomination's receipt in October 1987. The NRHP historic-name line reads 'Narracnaaqasras' under OCR, which looks like OCR damage for Narraguagus; not used. Lighthouse Friends dates Elizabeth Hitchcock's contact with the Gotts to 'around the turn of the nineteenth century', but the Gott tenure is 1893-1918; the story gives no date for it. The Dutcher letter (1900) is quoted by Lighthouse Friends; the original was not read. Elizabeth Hitchcock's recollections are quoted by Lighthouse Friends without a named source; the original was not read, so the story cites Lighthouse Friends only and paraphrases. Name variant: the Bulletin spells the first assistant 'Earle' in one place and 'Earl' in another; the story uses 'Earl'. Name trap: Pond Island in Maine also has another light (us-me-pond-island, a different island); this story is about Pond Island in Narraguagus Bay only. Charles E. Tracy's Boon Island assignment (Lighthouse Friends) is not added to other_stations because the sources give no years for it. Chronicling America newspaper searches for Narraguagus 1929-1934 returned no hits, and the 1887 page read had no relevant item. No wreck or rescue before 1929 is tied to the station in the sources read. The record's focal height 16.5 m matches the Archive's 54 ft; the record's NRHP date 20 Nov 1987 was not read on the NPGallery page. The record's nomination link is a NARA catalog address; it is not cited, per the guide.
